authority: 2026-10-11 owner: D24/D48/D96/... full peer numeric domains; extend THEIR laws to mathematical NEG and reduced RATIO compositions, never invent signed/rational domains or overwrite their complete natural atom range
rules: D24, D48, D96, D192, ... are first-class numeric DOMAINS with the same ontology rank as D1-D9.
The domain law is D(24 * 2^n), n >= 0; first width 24 and subsequent widths double.
A numeric object is exact bits + explicit numeric domain + admitted domain law, never an unqualified Number24 tier.
Equality of bit payload or mathematical magnitude cannot implicitly identify different domains; bridges require an independent law.
Numeric source literals and Text7 digits are optional surface projections, not semantic requirements.

For addition of two admitted nonnegative values in the SAME Dn numeric domain, compute the exact sum, including carry. If it fits n bits the result stays in Dn; if it needs n+1 bits it is admitted in next numeric domain D(2n), with all bits preserved. This is an explicit same-domain-addition bridge only.
Domain-qualified output retains its exact width, zero-filling unused high bits of the D(2n) word; zero-fill does not change its domain identity.
All 2^n base Dn bitwords still designate exact nonnegative natural atoms 0..2^n-1; no payload bit is stolen for sign, denominator or tag.

Signed integers and non-integral rationals are canonical domain-relative COMPOSITIONS of admitted Dn natural atoms under existing numeric-domain law, not additional n-bit atoms; finite Dn cannot injectively encode all integers or fractions and all 2^n naturals into its n-bit words.

NEG(x) admits strictly positive Dn natural magnitude x; NEG(0) is normalized to Dn zero and must never persist as a second negative zero. NEG does not redefine the n-bit magnitude payload and is not yet an executable opcode.

RATIO(p,q) has strictly positive natural denominator q, signed-or-natural numerator p, and must be reduced by gcd(abs(p),q)=1. Zero numerator canonicalizes to zero; denominator one canonicalizes to the signed-or-natural integer. A non-integral rational has denominator >1.

Each RATIO component preserves its own explicitly admitted Dn numeric-domain identity; gcd normalization rewrites magnitudes within these existing domains without implicit numeric-domain coercion. Equality of rational magnitudes does not itself alias different domain-qualified identities.

NEG and gcd-reduced RATIO remain compositions over existing admitted Dn atoms, never new domains, stolen n-bit payload bits or source literals. Core now executes canonical negative and fractional Values through already admitted + - * / and D1 comparisons on same-Dn operands, but no new binary opcode, physical reader, FASL/wire composite encoding, mixed-Dn arithmetic or external kernel is admitted.
Same-domain Dn natural multiplication is exact: if product fits n bits retain Dn, otherwise use next D(2n), since two n-bit natural operands have product width at most 2n. Never truncate or wrap.

Same-domain nonnegative natural subtraction retains Dn. A negative difference belongs to canonical NEG composition and must not be returned as an n-bit wrapped natural, nor called executable before a canonical NEG Value path exists.

Same-domain Dn Euclidean division by a nonzero divisor yields exact Dn quotient and Dn remainder (a=b*q+r, 0<=r<b). Exact zero-remainder quotient is a Dn natural; nonzero remainder requires the canonical reduced RATIO composition and cannot be rounded to a natural.
No same-Dn multiplication/subtraction/division permission implies a new mixed-Dn coercion, n-ary operation, signed/rational Value transport or operation opcode.
